summary: A superhero-themed 7th birthday for about 25 kids in Pune on a ₹60,000 budget, built around a two-hour 'Superhero Academy' with an obstacle course, mask and cape crafts, and a rescue-the-city treasure hunt. We assumed a society clubhouse or small party hall, around 10 accompanying parents, a vegetarian kid-friendly menu, and an afternoon slot so the kids are fresh. With roughly a month to go, booking the venue and entertainer and ordering the custom cake in the first week keeps everything comfortable.

budget.tips: Use a society clubhouse or community hall in Baner, Aundh or Kothrud with a weekday-evening or Sunday-morning rate instead of a commercial play zone, and ask for tables and chairs to be included.
Order a kids' menu of mini pizzas, veg sliders and pav bhaji bites from a home caterer at about ₹350 per head and serve parents tea and snacks from the same order.
Order one two-kg superhero cake from a local home baker and add a 'Kryptonite' green jelly cup station instead of a second cake.
Buy red, blue and yellow balloons in bulk from Tulshibaug, make a building skyline backdrop from printed chart paper, and reuse the same props as the photo booth.
Hire one host or a costumed superhero for 90 minutes and run the rest of the games yourself with a few volunteer relatives.
Give each child the cape or mask they made plus a small stationery set at around ₹180 per kid instead of buying toys.
Hire a photographer for one hour for the cake cutting and group photos and ask a relative to capture the games on a phone.
Send a WhatsApp invite card to parents, and keep a small kit of wipes, plasters and extra bags for spills and scrapes.
Keep this in cash for an extra guest count, an unexpected cake upgrade or a missing prop on the day.

timeline.task: Fix the date, time and guest list with the birthday boy and confirm the party theme and character
Book the clubhouse or hall in Pune and confirm table, chair and sound system access
Book the host or costumed superhero for a 90-minute slot
Send WhatsApp invitations to parents and ask for RSVPs and any food allergies
Order the custom superhero cake and confirm the design and delivery time
Finalise the kids' menu and place the catering order
Plan the Superhero Academy: obstacle course, mask and cape crafts and treasure hunt clues
Buy decor: balloons, banners, cape and mask materials and photo booth props
Prepare return gifts and goody bags with name tags
Confirm the final headcount and send a reminder with the venue pin to parents
Print treasure hunt clues, test the music playlist and pack the party kit
Decorate the hall two hours early, run the Superhero Academy games and cut the cake
Settle payments, return rented items and send thank-you notes with photos to parents

checklist: Confirm the time slot including set-up and clear-down
Check that chairs, tables, power sockets and a sound system are included
Ask whether outside caterers and decorators are allowed
Note the rules for balloons, confetti and wall decorations
Agree a veg kids' menu with mini pizza, sliders and pav bhaji bites
Ask for parents' tea, coffee and snacks to be added
Check for nut, dairy and gluten allergies from the RSVPs
Confirm delivery time, serving staff and disposable plates
Share a reference photo of the superhero design
Confirm weight, flavour and whether it is eggless
Agree on delivery time and an extra-careful packing note
Order the green jelly cups for the 'Kryptonite' dessert table
Buy balloons in red, blue and yellow and a helium option for the entrance arch
Prepare a city skyline backdrop and a photo booth with cutouts
Order or make capes and masks for every child
Plan the set-up time and who will help
Confirm the host or costumed superhero's time and set list
Agree on the 90-minute activity plan: obstacle course, craft and treasure hunt
Check that sound and a microphone are available
Plan prizes and a safe, supervised finish for each game

ideas.title: Superhero Academy training
ideas.description: Run a 'training' circuit with a cardboard shield obstacle course, a web-crawl under strings and a power-up water station. Every child earns a graduation badge.

ideas.title: Cape and mask workshop
ideas.description: Give each child a plain cape and mask to decorate with stickers and fabric markers. They wear their creation through the party and take it home as the return gift.

ideas.title: Save the city treasure hunt
ideas.description: Hide clue cards around the hall that spell out a secret code to 'save the city'. Teams of five kids solve them together, and the winning team opens the treasure box of stickers.

ideas.title: Kryptonite dessert table
ideas.description: Serve green jelly cups, popcorn 'power pellets' and juice labelled 'hero fuel' next to the cake so the food becomes part of the theme.

ideas.title: Birthday hero spotlight
ideas.description: Give the birthday boy a gold cape and a 'Hero of the Day' sash, and let his friends cheer as he receives a hand-made medal before the cake.
